video_title: Blazers Leaving Portland Becoming More Likely?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Deteriorating relationship between Portland politicians and the Blazers organization
quotes.excerpt: the rhetoric between the politicians and the Blazers organization is deteriorating

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: There is a story written by Bill Oram of the Portland Oregonian about the Blazers situation, which is getting worse by the day. The rhetoric between the politicians and the Blazers organization is deteriorating. Bill Oram got a hold of what he calls a top Blazers official. I don't know what that means, but the freedom with which this individual speaks with the kind of thrust that leads you to believe it's a very high Blazers official, and that it was certainly with the full blessing of Tom Dunden.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: And that it was certainly with the full blessing of Tom Dunden.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Portland Blazers board of directors meeting could signal team relocation
quotes.excerpt: it could be the declaration of all-out war

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: On Monday, the Blazers board of directors, which is essentially their owners, have a meeting. I have no idea what is going to come out of that meeting, but it could be the declaration of all-out war. This is a response to the city sending the Blazers what they wanted in the lease. They want the Blazers to sign a lease to get the money to renovate their arena.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers official expresses hostility toward unionized workforce and arena payments
quotes.excerpt: Why is the city sending this thing knowing we're not going to agree to it?
quotes.quote: Why is the city sending this thing knowing we're not going to agree to it? said the official, who expressed particular antipathy toward the unionized workforce and annual payment provisions. They want the unionized workforce and they want the Blazers to make annual $3 million payments. He expressed the opposite of support for the idea that they would have to use unionized labor. The city of Portland doesn't even recognize they got a sweetheart deal and they're making it complicated. And if they want to say no, if they don't want us, then that's fine.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers official claims relocation would not result in financial loss
quotes.excerpt: It's not like we lose money moving the team
quotes.quote: It's not like we lose money moving the team, the team official said. We might spend money, but we won't lose money. It might be okay to spend a billion dollars on a relocation fee if the value of the team doubles. Of course you would do that. They said it's okay for you to say this in the paper. This was clear.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers ownership complains about lack of local sponsorship
quotes.excerpt: they complained about the lack of sponsorship, local sponsorship and stuff

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: They complained about the lack of sponsorship, local sponsorship and stuff, but that's relatively small. And they also said that this deal is only going to get worse. Basically, the market sucks is what they're saying.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Basically, the market sucks and we don't want to be there anyway.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: This relationship has not been good from the beginning.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Historical context of Blazers ownership's desire to relocate
quotes.excerpt: there was an email that was sent in between the owners where they basically were saying
quotes.quote: At one point Aubrey McClendon, who has since passed away, he was Clay Bennett's friend and partner. There was an email that was sent in between the owners where they basically were saying, okay, we got the team, now let's move it, essentially. And that was seen as inflammatory. But that was a private email that got released. This is on the record in the newspaper.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers broadcast crew changes and Kevin Calabro's departure
quotes.excerpt: they let the radio voices go
quotes.quote: Their broadcast crew, a lot of whom had been there for a lot of years, they let the radio voices go. Kevin Calabro, who's been with them for 10 years. Kevin Calabro was the voice of the Sonics. The Sonics moved, he became an ESPN, he'd call games for ESPN college and NBA on ESPN. Actually left ESPN because he wanted to call games for a team again. And with the Blazers job came open and I remember talking to him when he left. He was like, yeah, this is a tough decision and in some people would say that this was a step back, but I love being the voice of a team and I'm going to go do it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers offered Kevin Calabro a subprime contract
quotes.excerpt: they offered him a contract that he said on the record was quote subprime
quotes.quote: They offered him a contract that he said on the record was quote subprime, which I thought was a shot across the bow. Because Tom Dunden was known for giving subprime auto loans. That's one of his businesses.
